text: In the one day since the last run, beauty gained about 16,900 new reviews, four times any other category, led by a ₹138 Wildplay perfume (+2,478) and a Mamaearth face wash (+1,574), with health (+4,191) and home & kitchen (+3,052) next. For a beginner, home & kitchen and jewellery still look best: ₹91 to ₹101 fridge covers keep climbing (+742, +321) and jewellery stays light, cheap and low on complaints, while kids' winter wear is a good second choice.

headline: Women's ethnic: kurtis keep selling, net and silk sarees join the page
text: Kurtis still have the most reviews, and a ₹237 kurti (+147) and a ₹200 kurti (+117) gained the most in the last day, with a ₹384 shimmer saree with mirror work (+109) close behind. Eight listings are new to the page, mostly net, organza, Banarasi and Kasavu sarees, which fits Diwali on 8 November and the wedding season that starts later this month. The typical price is about ₹298, and about 9.2% of reviews are 1-star. Gujarat and Rajasthan sellers lead, so price competition is strong. Free-size sarees are easier than sized kurtis, but stock bought now would arrive after Diwali, so aim at wedding season instead.

headline: Women's western: shirts and tank tops lead, jackets climb with winter
text: A ₹194 women's shirt gained the most reviews in the last day (+155), followed by a ₹165 tank top (+140) and a ₹294 girls' jacket (+136). A white crop jacket is also new to the page, so winter layers are picking up. The typical price is about ₹271, with about 7.4% 1-star reviews, lower than most clothing here. Delhi sellers lead by a wide margin (24 of 40 products). Sizes still mean returns, so start with a small range of tops in free or few sizes.

headline: Men's clothing: slowest category, shirts lead and sweatshirts arrive
text: Men's clothing again gained the fewest new reviews, only about 240 in a day, mostly on shirts priced ₹248 to ₹352. Hoodies, sweaters and fleece sweatshirts are new or rising on the page, which fits the start of winter, but they have only a few hundred to about 1,300 reviews so far. About 11.5% of reviews are 1-star, the second-highest after electronics, which points to quality complaints and returns. The typical price is about ₹282, and Punjab and Delhi sellers lead. It is not a good first category unless you have a reliable supplier.

headline: Kids & toys: cheap clothing sets and winter basics keep moving
text: Kids gained about 2,900 new reviews in a day, led by a ₹182 three-pack cat print set (+324), a ₹189 boys' set (+261), a ₹203 kids' sweater set (+244) and ₹121 baby socks (+213). New to the page are thermal sets, a plush school bag, a ₹221 pull-back police car and flashcards. The typical price is low at about ₹178, with about 8.6% 1-star reviews. Gujarat and Delhi sellers lead. Toys, socks and flashcards need no sizes, so they are the easier start, and Children's Day (14 November) and Christmas can help small toys.

headline: Home & kitchen: fridge covers are the fastest movers again
text: Three fridge covers priced ₹91 to ₹101 gained the most reviews in the last day (+742, +321 and +297), followed by ₹73 incense sticks (+281) and an ₹80 Premanand Ji wall hanging (+255). The category gained about 3,050 new reviews, third after beauty and health. New to the page are kitchen tools such as a masher, a masala box and air fryer trays. The typical price is the lowest here at about ₹148, with about 7.3% 1-star reviews, and Delhi and Gujarat sellers lead. Light, no sizes and few complaints make this the best start, though incense and pooja items may slow after Diwali.

headline: Beauty: cheap perfumes lead again, but big brands dominate
text: Beauty gained about 16,900 new reviews in a day, by far the most of any category. A ₹138 Wildplay perfume (+2,478), a ₹221 Mamaearth face wash (+1,574), a Ghar Soaps face wash (+1,561) and a ₹144 French Essence body spray (+1,494) moved most. Most top products are brands such as Ghar Soaps, Muuchstac, Mamaearth, Nivea and Vaseline. The typical price is about ₹189 with about 8.3% 1-star reviews, and Haryana and Maharashtra sellers lead. Branded items usually need brand approval, so a beginner would need their own small unbranded or private-label product, such as a body spray, to compete.

headline: Jewellery: light, cheap and set up for wedding season
text: A ₹142 rhodium plated set with Austrian diamonds gained the most reviews in the last day (+307), followed by a ₹151 golden bracelet (+128) and a ₹163 silver plated necklace set (+89). Eight listings are new to the page, including toe rings, layered necklaces and jewellery sets, and mangalsutras and stud earrings are rising. The typical price is about ₹189 with about 7.9% 1-star reviews, and Gujarat and Maharashtra sellers lead. Jewellery is light, has no sizes and needs no brand licence, and wedding season starting later in November should help sets and mangalsutras.

headline: Bags & footwear: handbags and sling bags lead, shoes need sizes
text: Handbags have the most reviews, and a ₹151 sling bag (+109), a ₹166 printed tote (+83) and a ₹251 handbag (+76) gained the most in the last day. A ₹114 men's wallet (+75) is also rising. New to the page are several handbags, slippers and juttis. The typical price is about ₹203 with about 7.5% 1-star reviews, and Delhi sellers lead strongly (25 of 40). Bags have no sizes and are a good start, while footwear needs sizes and usually brings more returns.

headline: Electronics accessories: speakers lead, highest complaint rate
text: Bluetooth speakers have the most reviews, and a ₹382 wooden speaker (+165), an ₹84 phone stand two-pack (+124) and a ₹282 speaker (+82) gained the most in the last day. A ₹101 cable protector (+80) is also rising, and new listings include mini speakers and 'AirPods Pro' style earbuds, which carry brand-copy risk. The typical price is the highest here at about ₹334, and about 11.6% of reviews are 1-star, the highest of all categories. Delhi, Gujarat and Haryana sellers lead. Simple items like phone stands and cable protectors are fine, but avoid gadgets that can stop working.

headline: Health & fitness: brands lead pads, ear patches are the easy pick
text: Health gained about 4,190 new reviews in a day, second only to beauty, led by a ₹128 Dabur Red toothpaste combo (+1,076), Everteen and Stayfree pads (+421, +358) and ₹68 earlobe support patches (+410). New and rising are sports items such as footballs, cricket balls, bat grips and badminton rackets. The typical price is about ₹214, and only about 5.5% of reviews are 1-star, the lowest of all categories. Delhi and Uttar Pradesh sellers lead. Branded pads and toothpaste are hard to compete with, but earlobe patches, ear cleaners and small sports items like bat grips are light and unbranded.

Fridge covers around ₹90 to ₹100 (home & kitchen, fastest movers again)
American diamond or rhodium plated jewellery sets around ₹140 to ₹190 (wedding season ahead)
Sling bags and printed tote bags around ₹150 to ₹170
Kids' socks packs and simple winter sets around ₹120 to ₹200
Invisible earlobe support patches around ₹70
Phone stands and cable protectors around ₹80 to ₹100

Avoid for now: men's shirts (slow growth and 11.5% 1-star reviews), earbuds and speakers (highest complaint rate and copy-brand risk), branded beauty and sanitary products, and festive-only Diwali stock that would arrive too late.
